dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: A proposition on real-valued functions. Through its constructor D002, it packages the assertions that the function is nonnegative almost everywhere, vanishes almost everywhere on the negative half-line, is at most 1 almost everywhere on the nonnegative half-line, is integrable with respect to real volume measure, and has integral 1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the substantive hypothesis on f and supplies the density-like support, boundedness, integrability, and normalization conditions used by the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: Constructor for LocalDef001: for f : Real → Real, it takes five premises—f ≥ 0 almost everywhere; for almost every x, x < 0 implies f(x) = 0; for almost every x, 0 ≤ x implies f(x) ≤ 1; f is integrable for real volume measure; and the integral of f is 1—and yields LocalDef001 f.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes the exact content of the otherwise opaque LocalDef001 assumption and shows that the target applies only to normalized, nonnegative, essentially supported-on-[0,∞), essentially 1-bounded integrable functions.

hypotheses: The function f satisfies LocalDef001: f is nonnegative almost everywhere with respect to real volume measure.
The function f vanishes almost everywhere on the negative half-line: for almost every x, x < 0 implies f(x) = 0.
The function f is at most 1 almost everywhere on the nonnegative half-line: for almost every x, 0 ≤ x implies f(x) ≤ 1.
The function f is integrable with respect to real volume measure.
The integral of f over the real line is exactly 1.
The parameter t is strictly positive.
conclusions: The weighted integral over the real line satisfies ∫_ℝ exp(-t x) f(x) dx ≤ 1/t.
mathematical_definitions: All integrals and almost-everywhere assertions use the canonical volume measure on ℝ.
LocalDef001 f is the density-like package supplied by D002: f ≥ 0 almost everywhere, f = 0 almost everywhere for x < 0, f ≤ 1 almost everywhere for x ≥ 0, f is integrable, and ∫_ℝ f(x) dx = 1.
The exponential weight is the ordinary real function x ↦ e^{-t x}.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every integrable real function f that is a nonnegative, normalized density with respect to real volume measure, is supported on the nonnegative half-line up to null sets, and is bounded above by 1 there up to null sets, and for every real t > 0, its exponentially damped integral is at most 1/t: ∫_ℝ e^{-t x} f(x) dx ≤ 1/t.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The claim is restricted to real-valued functions on the real line satisfying the bundled LocalDef001 conditions; it is not stated for arbitrary measures, densities with a different essential bound, or support on another half-line.
The support, nonnegativity, and upper-bound conditions hold only almost everywhere, so changing f on a null set does not affect applicability.
The parameter range is strictly t > 0; t = 0 and negative t are excluded.
The conclusion is only an upper bound and does not assert equality, sharpness, or a lower bound.

The weighted integrand's integrability is not separately present as a conclusion-level hypothesis, although the bundled assumptions on f together with t > 0 make the intended weighted integral well behaved.
There is no evident vacuity: standard nonnegative functions supported on an interval of length 1 and equal to 1 there satisfy the displayed density-like conditions up to endpoints.
ambiguities: The one-level body of MeasureTheory.integral is opaque in the dossier, so its behavior on nonintegrable functions is not independently recoverable here; this appears immaterial under the LocalDef001 conditions and t > 0.
The dossier identifies the canonical real volume-measure instance structurally but does not expand it to a foundational construction; the translation treats it as the standard volume measure on ℝ.
